label: Resistance from geometry
subgoals: Compute the cross-section from width and copper weight
Apply R equals rho L over A in consistent units
Estimate resistance from squares times sheet resistance

label: Voltage drop on power traces
subgoals: Multiply current by trace resistance to get the drop
Compare the drop with the rail's tolerance
Replace a trace with a plane or remote sense when the drop is too large

label: Temperature and frequency effects
subgoals: Scale resistance to the operating temperature
Check a voltage-drop budget at the hot corner
Recognize when skin effect makes DC resistance a lower bound
